$comment: Fill before the first translation pass; the empty primary pair and ellipsis glyph fail i18n-mechanics until you do. Take every choice from what the language's macOS writes (the reference pile), and say where in this comment. Schema and macros: docs/i18n/termbase.md § <tag>/mechanics.json schema. Worked examples to adapt, each an entry for "spacing" or "hedges": (1) the percent sign, when the language spaces it (de 42 %): { "pattern": "[\\d\\uFFFC]%", "why": "a space goes before % (42 %)" }; when it writes it tight (hu 42%): { "pattern": "[\\d\\uFFFC] %", "why": "% hugs its number (42%)" }. (2) the English multiplier 4x, which most languages spell out (fr 4 fois, es 4 veces): { "pattern": "\\b\\d+x\\b", "why": "a multiplier spells out the word (4 fois), never 4x" }. (3) a suffix glued to a name Cmdr can't know (hu {name}-ban, sv {name}s), which {@name} targets without catching counts or Cmdr's own tokens: { "pattern": "{@name}-?\\p{Ll}", "why": "a suffix on an unknown name depends on its sound; use a colon slot or a postposition" }. (4) a bracketed plural ending (fr fichier(s)): { "pattern": "\\p{L}\\((?:s|es)\\)", "why": "a bracketed plural; use ICU plural, or rephrase" }.
